items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I would ask my aunt, Edna May Sanders, 'Am I doing it right?' or 'Am I correct?' or 'Is it a good idea to do it this or that way?'

ctx.x: Yeah. In the muscles, you see. And then, as I said, we were still growing lads, and that's what he did. And all during these times I was very inquisitive, you see, because whenever I wanted anything explained to me that I thought wasn't an actual fact, I would ask my aunt, Edna May Sanders, 'Am I doing it right?' or 'Am I correct?' or 'Is it a good idea to do it this or that way?' you know. So I had -- actually I had three -- well, four teachers, I mean

to myself they were teachers, because I would ask Tiger Flowers questions about, like rhythms, you know, and he would always say, "Well, I'm the student and you're teacher." He couldn't explain the rhythms to me, the way that Mr. Bubbles did, or either J.D., Chuckles.
